So, Marcelo. If your company gave you a year off tomorrow, what would you do?
Honestly? I would cycle from Patagonia to Peru. I daydream about it on every long ride.
Would you uproot the family for that?
No. That would be a pipe dream. Realistically, they would stay, and I would go for three months, not twelve.
And the job? Some people say they would never take the year, because they would worry too much.
That is the trade-off. If I were thirty, I might not take it. At my age, the risk is smaller than the regret.
So is it a plan, or wishful thinking?
A plan, I think. Our company offers sabbaticals after fifteen years. If they approve it, I will go in 2028.

Marcelo, hi, it is Fiona. Your interview was great, by the way. My editor loved the part about the plateau. Now I have a second question for the same piece, and I would like you to think about it before we talk. If your company offered you a year off tomorrow, fully paid, what would you do with it? Would you stay in São Paulo, or would you uproot the whole family? Some people tell me they would cycle across a continent. Others say they would never take it, because they would be too worried about the job. I want an honest answer, not a pipe dream. Think about it, and call me on Thursday.

Welcome back to The Long Game. Today, a small grammar point with a big effect on how we decide. Listen to these two sentences. If I get the job, I will move to Lisbon. If I got the job, I would move to Lisbon. The first one is a plan. The speaker thinks it can happen, so he is already preparing. The second one is a daydream, or at least a hypothesis. The speaker is imagining, not planning. Here is the interesting part. People who talk about their goals in the second conditional for years usually never do anything. At some point, the would has to become a will. So listen to yourself this week. If you are always saying, if I had more time, I would, ask yourself a simple question. Realistically, is that a plan, or is it wishful thinking?

First, I imagine the situation with if and the past. Then, I say what I would do. Next, I weigh the pros and cons. After that, I say what the trade-off would be. Finally, I decide whether it is a real plan or a daydream.
